name: workspace-theme
description: Apply a full color theme per workspace folder, from a single path-to-theme map in your user settings.

workspaceTheme.themes.markdownDescription:
**Quick actions:** [Set workspace theme](command:workspaceTheme.pickThemeForWorkspace) | [Delete workspace theme](command:workspaceTheme.useGlobalTheme) | [Edit mapping](command:workspaceTheme.editMapping)

___

Map of folder path (or path prefix) to a color theme label. When a matching folder is opened, that full theme is written to the folder's workspace settings. Longest-prefix match wins, so `/home/you` can set a default while `/home/you/project-b` overrides it.

Example:
```json
{
  "/home/you/project-a": "Mint Green",
  "/home/you/project-b": "Tomorrow Night Blue"
}
```

additionalProperties.markdownDescription: Color theme label exactly as it appears in the theme picker (e.g. "Mint Green"). Tip: use **Set workspace theme** to choose it with a live preview instead of typing it here.

workspaceTheme.autoGitExclude.markdownDescription: Because applying a per-workspace theme creates/edits `.vscode/settings.json` **inside the project folder** - a file that is usually part of a shared git repo - this keeps your personal theme from being committed. When that file is not already ignored, it is added to `.git/info/exclude` (a **local, untracked** ignore that never modifies the shared `.gitignore`). Turn this off if you actually want the workspace theme committed to the repo.
